PG4 threshold convergence (2026-09-15): the sub-100 ns lean rows carry widened per-target thresholds (warn 30% / fail 60%) because isolated local reruns measured them across a ~1.9x range (docs/benchmarks/2026-09-10-o1-lean-isolated-repeats.csv); the >=200 ns rows are stable and keep the global 15/30. The overrides are also the guardrails for the first CI-native capture; tighten them once real CI variance is known.

small benchmarks (docs/benchmarks/2026-09-10-o1-lean-isolated-repeats.csv) measured MEOP between
19.5 and 46.8 ns and the lean path between 30.5 and 59.2 ns, i.e. the lean path tracks MEOP within a
factor of roughly 1.0-1.6. Treat the absolute figures as order-of-magnitude comparisons; the
allocation column of the lean path (0 B per synchronous round-trip) is the reproducible part.
Allocation figures for the general-purpose engine fluctuate between runs (0-1065 B) because the
first measured iterations amortise lazily created internal structures over the operation count.
Absolute values are machine dependent: comparing a GitHub runner against this file is a cross-environment
comparison. Until a CI-captured baseline is committed (see docs/benchmarks/baseline/README.md), treat results
as advisory (calibration = true) and prefer the ratio-based reference rows over absolute thresholds.
Only entries with gated = true participate in the pass/fail gate; reference rows are reported for context.
The Concurrent-100 suite is recorded but never gated (observed run-to-run variance is far above the thresholds).

Gate policy (Q1, 2026-09-15): this file is the calibration-mode baseline. Committing a CI-native capture (workflow `update_baseline` input -> ci-baseline artifact) replaces this file with calibration = false, which switches the workflow from advisory to enforcing: failMeanPercent and the allocFailBytes gate then block. Until then the workflow stays advisory by design, not by omission.
